title: Retrospective test: OpenAI's corrected cone claim (Taming implies compatibility on four-manifolds)
source: openai/math @ fd4aeeb; history.md (Oct 7, 2026 fixes); preprint versions September-23-2026 (original) and October-6-2026 (corrected)
what_openai_corrected: Original Corollary (Taming and compatible cones) claimed K^t = K^c + H_J^- for every closed 4-manifold, and K^t = K^c when b2+ = 1, citing Li-Zhang 2009 Corollary 1.1. Corrected version: cone-sum equality only when h_J^- = b2+ - 1; strict inclusion can occur (explicit four-torus example).
lean_scope: Only the main theorem (taming implies compatibility) is formalized: ComparatorChallenges/TamingCompatibility.lean. The cone corollary has no Lean statement.

test1_pipeline_audit_blind.result: Main theorem judged equivalent to the Lean statement; the cone corollary marked not_formalized (low-severity coverage flag). The later-corrected claim lies entirely in the part the pipeline marks as awaiting formal verification.

test2_ai_referee_blind.result: Judged the original proof sound; recalled the cited Li-Zhang result as unconditional. It missed the error OpenAI later corrected.
test2_ai_referee_blind.note: One ad-hoc Opus call asking it to check each step of the original corollary's proof; the prompt was not saved, only the answer.

contamination: Correction published Oct 7, 2026, after the model's training cutoff (about June 2026); the prompts contain only the original text.
other_corrections: 3 withdrawn manuscripts had no Lean formalization. Incompressible Box Transport (repaired estimates) is formalized; whether the repaired estimates were inside its Lean scope was not checked. Other corrected manuscripts have no matching scope note.
takeaway: The one statement-level error OpenAI corrected in a formalized result sat outside the Lean-verified statement, exactly where the pipeline places a 'not formally verified' sticky note. An AI referee reading the flawed proof called it sound: AI judgment is not a substitute for knowing what Lean actually verified.
